summary: Tested the 'Admin - Global Config' starting Model Vessel wizard. All 6 backend pytest checks passed. UI scenarios A-E were run with test-user-pro on a 390px mobile viewport, and all passed. A: Basic not finished, last used = route planning, fresh copy -> 'TRAINING · STEP 1 OF 6' (Basic, not Route Planning). Next and reload stay on Basic, step 2. B: Basic finished -> 'ROUTE PLANNING · STEP 1 OF 28'. C: localStorage cleared, Basic not finished -> Basic step 1. D: Help > Model Vessel > Crew Registration and Invites -> step 1 of 14; Next -> step 2; reload keeps Crew Registration step 2. E: config line changed to Crew Safety Briefings -> 'CREW SAFETY BRIEFINGS · STEP 1 OF 16'. One minor race: in E, Basic shows for about 150ms first, then switches.

integration_issues.flow: Fresh Model Vessel copy on a device that has never loaded the Global Config or wizards-done lists
integration_issues.issue: TrainingMode uses start = startingWizard(useAdminLists(CONFIG)) || BASIC, and finished comes from useWizardsDone (localStorage cache, then GET /api/wizards/mine). Both load async, so the first render can show the wrong walkthrough. Seen in Scenario E: titles over time were ['TRAINING · STEP 1 OF 6', 'CREW SAFETY BRIEFINGS · STEP 1 OF 16']. The wizardEvent 'open' effect also fired for Basic: db.wizard_progress basic opens went up by 1 for a walkthrough that was never really shown. Analytics gets an extra open. If the user presses Next during that short window, go() locks the wrong walkthrough (fresh=false). The same race can happen in Scenario B (finished=[] before /wizards/mine returns), but it did not show in my run.

action_items: Minor: on a fresh copy, wait to render the wizard and send the 'open' wizardEvent until the CONFIG admin list and /wizards/mine have loaded at least once (or until a cached value exists). This stops the short Basic flash, the extra Basic open count and an accidental lock-in.
critical_code_review_comments: TrainingMode.jsx: pick = fresh && !finished.includes(start) ? start : which || start is correct. go() clears fresh on the first move, and restartWalkthrough sets fresh=false. The logic matches the user's rule.
When copy is '' (model_copy is missing because created_at is missing), the reset never runs. That is fine because server.py always sends created_at for model boats.
On a new device with Basic finished and no last-used walkthrough, which='' falls back to start (Basic). That matches the rule.
